title: Mirror coordinates inside a random intrinsic subspace
hypothesis: One fitted angle per task inside a random intrinsic subspace preserves aligned held-out predictions with lower total payload than standard SAID and direct two-coordinate coefficients; arbitrary intrinsic codes require richer state.
physical_object: fixed 16-parameter predictor plus a shared paid 16x4 random orthonormal projection basis
mirror_coordinate: per-task FP16 angle on a fixed-radius circle in the first two intrinsic coordinates
logical_multiplicity: 64 task-conditioned linear functions; the task count is not treated as independent capacity
controls: PA33 random-subspace SAID with four FP32 codes/task
same-plane two-coefficient code with two FP16 values/task

data.unrelated_teacher: theta_t = theta0 + P @ z_t, z_t independently Gaussian in R^4

selection.tunable: none; 720-point angle grid, precision, dimensions and code families are frozen

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes after reload

success_gate: All 3 development aligned worlds: Mirror normalized test MSE <=1e-4; within 1e-5 absolute normalized MSE of direct two-coefficient control; Mirror total bytes <=75% PA33 SAID and <=90% two-coefficient control.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality or either byte gate, or one-angle coordinates fail unrelated tasks without an aligned useful byte-quality point.

fresh.open_condition: only if all development aligned quality and byte gates are met
